title: Gender-Sensitive Care for Patients with Non-Cystic Fibrosis Bronchiectasis: An Online Survey on Subjective Experiences, Sex- and Gender-Related Influences, and Hormonal Life Stages
summary:
Background: Bronchiectasis is a chronic lung condition in which the airways become permanently widened, leading to repeated infections, ongoing cough, and increased mucus production. Little is currently known about whether the condition presents differently in women, men, and other genders, or whether physical changes over the course of life, such as during puberty, pregnancy, or menopause, affect the symptoms.

Research question: Do people with this lung condition have different experiences regarding diagnosis, treatment, and daily life with the condition depending on their sex or gender? And are certain life stages linked to changes in symptoms?

Methodology: Adults with a doctor-confirmed diagnosis of this lung condition (not caused by cystic fibrosis) are invited to take part voluntarily and anonymously in an online survey. Completing it takes about 10 to 15 minutes. No physical examinations are performed and no samples need to be provided. Responses are only summarized and analyzed anonymously; individual participants cannot be identified.

interventions.name: Single-arm, non-interventional observational study without a comparison group. Participants access the anonymous online survey on the LimeSurvey platform via a QR code (flyer) or link. Inclusion criteria:

Exclusion criteria:
Bronchiectasis caused by cystic fibrosis
Insufficient knowledge of the German language
Lack of capacity to consent
